why: This repository is public and the scanner is the only thing standing between a pasted terminal transcript and a committed subscription id. Every edit below leaves it exiting 0 on a tree that carries an identifier: a rule deleted, an exemption widened until it exempts nearly every real GUID, a scan that reached no content, or a verdict computed and then thrown away.

mutations.name: the GUID rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: Subscription and tenant ids are the usual leak, and the rule that catches them stops recording anything.

mutations.name: the synthetic-fixture exemption is widened to 15
mutations.breaks: The exemption for obviously-fake GUIDs becomes an exemption for about nineteen in twenty real ones. No rule is deleted and nothing else changes.

mutations.name: the AKS API-server FQDN rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: A per-cluster, per-tenant control-plane hostname sits in the tree with no symptom.

mutations.name: the ACR rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: A literal registry login server names live infrastructure and invites squatting on the registry name.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, n, "literal ACR login server", m.group(0)))

mutations.name: the cloudapp DNS-label rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: The public edge's DNS label names a load balancer somebody else can later own.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, n, "literal public DNS label (cloudapp.azure.com)", m.group(0)))

mutations.name: the Azure Monitor workspace rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: A workspace resource id ends in the workspace name — the half a shape rule can see, and the half that names the tenant's observability estate.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, n, "literal Azure Monitor workspace resource id", m.group(0)))

mutations.name: the Log Analytics workspace rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: There are two workspace kinds with two rules; deleting one leaves the other looking like coverage for both.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, n, "literal Log Analytics workspace resource id", m.group(0)))

mutations.name: the monitor-endpoint rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: A Managed Prometheus query endpoint or a data-collection endpoint derives its hostname from the workspace name, so the hostname identifies the workspace as surely as its id does.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, n, "literal Azure Monitor endpoint (monitor.azure.com)", m.group(0)))

mutations.name: the public-IPv4 rule finds nothing
mutations.breaks: The edge's public address gets committed. The private and documentation ranges still pass, so the exemptions look tested while the rule they qualify does nothing.

mutations.name: an empty file list is reported as a clean tree
mutations.breaks: An enumeration that failed — a bad path, a git command that errored — becomes a pass. "Nothing to check" answers as "checked, found nothing".

mutations.name: a placeholder path is judged by its first component only
mutations.breaks: A parameterised-looking prefix carries a real workspace name behind it: ${AMW}.realname.westus3 reads as parameterised and passes.
mutations.find: return all(PLACEHOLDER.match(part) for part in name.split("."))

mutations.name: an unreadable file is skipped in silence
mutations.breaks: A permissions problem shrinks the scanned set with no symptom, and the report still reads clean.
mutations.find: findings.append((p, 0, "could not be read (not scanned)", str(e)))

mutations.name: findings are printed and then reported as clean
mutations.breaks: The scan is correct and its verdict is discarded: the output names every identifier and the exit code says the tree is fine, so CI stays green.
